sourcedFrom: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year)
cleanIntro: The Patrol is the A300 mechanism in a defensive gun, and its forend is the one thing that is genuinely different — it fits flush to the receiver and comes off in its own sequence. ⛔ And it carries a cleaning interval nothing else in the book does: slugs and buckshot lead up the gas system, and Beretta wants the gas parts cleaned every 200 rounds of it.

steps.title: Unloaded first, all three places checked
steps.action: Chamber, receiver and magazine, by eye through the ejection port, the loading gate and the chamber. On a gun kept for defence this matters more, not less — it has probably been sitting loaded.
steps.aside: It is advisable to carry out the disassembly operations over a table to catch components should they drop.
steps.quote: ALWAYS CHECK THAT THE SHOTGUN IS UNLOADED (EMPTY CARTRIDGE CHAMBER, EMPTY RECEIVER, EMPTY MAGAZINE). INSPECT THE FIREARM BY LOOKING THROUGH THE EJECTION PORT, THE LOADING GATE AND THE CHAMBER. IF IT IS NOT EMPTY, UNLOAD IT AS INSTRUCTED IN THE RELEVANT SECTION.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 PATROL DISASSEMBLY, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Carrier stop pressed, bolt locked to the rear
steps.action: Press the carrier stop push button if it is not already pressed, then lock the bolt back. Nothing comes off a gas gun with the bolt closed on a spring.
steps.aside: Lock the bolt to the rear.
steps.quote: Press the carrier stop push button, if it has not already been pressed.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 PATROL DISASSEMBLY, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Barrel clamp off, then the forend cap
steps.action: Loosen the two hex screws and take the barrel clamp off, then unscrew the forend cap anti-clockwise.
steps.aside: Unscrew forend cap in a counterclockwise direction.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel clamp by loosening the (2) hex screws.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 PATROL DISASSEMBLY, printed p.26-27

steps.title: ⛔ Magazine cap sleeve — note which way round it sits
steps.action: Take the magazine cap sleeve off the magazine tube, and note its orientation before it moves. The Patrol's flush forend depends on that sleeve going back the right way round, and Beretta prints the instruction because it will fit wrongly without complaint.
steps.quote: Remove the magazine cap sleeve from the magazine tube. NOTE: To aid in proper installation of the magazine cap sleeve, note the orientation of the sleeve before removal.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 PATROL DISASSEMBLY, printed p.26-27

steps.title: Forend forward, adapter off, barrel out — strip complete
steps.action: Slide the forend toward the muzzle and take the barrel assembly out of the receiver; with the barrel off, the forend adapter / piston stop comes away. ⛔ Keep clear of the valve: its spring and retaining nut are never removed.
steps.aside: With the barrel assembly off the forend adapter/piston stop can now be removed.
steps.quote: Remove the barrel assembly from the receiver.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 PATROL DISASSEMBLY, printed p.26-27

steps.title: ⛔ Slugs and buck: clean the gas system every 200 rounds
steps.action: This is the Patrol's own maintenance rule and it appears nowhere else in the book. Firing slugs and buckshot leaves lead in the gas system, so Beretta asks for the gas cylinder, piston, ring and barrel to be cleaned every 200 rounds of that ammunition to keep the gun cycling. Birdshot practice does not carry the same interval.
steps.quote: Firing slugs and buck shot through the A300 Patrol can result in lead buildup in the gas operating system. Beretta recommends cleaning the gas cylinder, piston, ring, and barrel after every 200 rounds to ensure reliable function when firing these types of ammunition.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — DESCRIPTION — A300 Patrol, printed p.13

steps.title: Choke housing first — it is where the fouling packs in
steps.action: With the choke out, brush the housing clean and dry it, then check the choke itself inside AND outside. A thin film of gun oil goes on the barrel thread and the choke before it is screwed back — that is what stops a choke seizing in a gas gun after a season of hot loads.
steps.aside: Apply a thin film of Beretta Gun Oil on the barrel thread and choke tube.
steps.quote: Clean the choke housing thoroughly using, if necessary, a brush swab soaked with Beretta Gun Oil. Dry the housing with a soft cloth.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

steps.title: Barrel, and the barrel extension people forget
steps.action: Soft cloth patch through the bore for the combustion residue, brass brush or an oiled cloth if it needs more. Then clean the barrel EXTENSION thoroughly — that is the block the bolt locks into, and fouling there is what makes a semi-auto shotgun fail to go into battery. Dry patch, light oil, then check the bore is clear.
steps.aside: Carefully clean the inside of the barrel with a soft cloth patch to remove any combustion residue. If necessary, use a brass brush or a cloth soaked with Beretta Gun Oil.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

steps.title: ⛔ Gas cylinder and piston — clean, and then leave DRY
steps.action: Spray and clean the magazine tube shaft, and check the piston still glides freely along it. Brush the gas cylinder walls with a brass brush and wipe the residue out. ⛔ Then STOP: Beretta says never to oil inside the gas cylinder. Oil in there turns powder residue into a paste and that is the classic cause of a gas gun short-stroking.
steps.aside: Make sure that the piston glides freely on the magazine tube shaft.
steps.quote: To clean the walls of the gas cylinder, clean thoroughly with a brass brush.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

steps.title: ⛔ The exhaust valve is self-cleaning — hands off
steps.action: The valve device that bleeds excess gas is self-cleaning and Beretta wants it left alone: never remove its spring or its retaining nut, and never take the assembly apart. If something is genuinely wrong with it, that is a gunsmith's job. This is a published DON'T and this guide does not go round it.
steps.aside: NEVER REMOVE the spring of the valve or the valve retaining nut. The valve device is self-cleaning and requires no maintenance. If necessary, contact a competent gunsmith.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE the exhaust valve assembly. If necessary, contact a competent gunsmith.
steps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — ROUTINE MAINTENANCE, printed p.36

deepSteps.title: Bolt strip is for cleaning only — the book says so first
deepSteps.action: Beretta prefaces the bolt strip with the reason for it: the breech bolt assembly only comes apart in order to clean its components. It is not an inspection ritual and it is not something to do after every box of shells — end of season, or when the gun has been wet or filthy.
deepSteps.aside: Its loading, unloading and maintenance are identical to the rest of the A300 family as detailed in this manual.
deepSteps.quote: The breech bolt assembly only needs to be disassembled in order to clean its components.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 ULTIMA DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23-25

deepSteps.title: Cocking handle out — it comes hard, and that is normal
deepSteps.action: With the barrel off, ride the bolt forward under control with a finger on the cocking handle while you press the release button, then pull the cocking handle straight out. It takes real force. People stop pulling because they think something is wrong; nothing is.
deepSteps.aside: Pulling forcefully, extract the cocking handle from the breech bolt.
deepSteps.quote: Holding the cocking handle, press the breech bolt release button and gently guide the breech bolt forward to the locked position.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 ULTIMA DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23-25

deepSteps.title: Bolt assembly forward off the magazine tube shaft
deepSteps.action: Work over a flat surface with the ejection port UP, then slide the connecting rod and sleeve forward off the magazine tube shaft to draw the bolt assembly out of the receiver. Ejection port up is not a detail: it keeps the firing pin, locking block and springs in the bolt instead of on the floor.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: The breech bolt assembly, no longer held by the connecting rod with sleeve, will divide into:
deepSteps.quote: Over a flat surface, with the ejection port pointed upwards, slide the connecting rod with sleeve forward off the magazine tube shaft to extract the breech bolt assembly from the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 ULTIMA DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23-25

deepSteps.title: Trigger pack out with the trigger guard as the lever
deepSteps.action: Drive the trigger guard retaining pin out with a punch or an awl, then lever the trigger pack out of the receiver by the trigger guard — first toward the barrel, then outward. Two directions, in that order; pulling straight down is what breaks trigger guards.
deepSteps.aside: With the breech bolt in the closed position, engage the safety (red ring not visible).
deepSteps.quote: Using a pin punch or an awl, Remove the trigger guard retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 ULTIMA DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23-25

deepSteps.title: Clean the pack and the receiver, then lubricate lightly
deepSteps.action: Soft cloth over the trigger pack, then a light film on all the metal components AND on the trigger pack retaining pin. Do the receiver the same way as the bolt, and lubricate the internal breech bolt guides — those rails are what the bolt runs on.
deepSteps.aside: Clean thoroughly with a soft cloth and lubricate the internal breech bolt guides.
deepSteps.quote: Lightly lubricate all the metal components and the trigger pack retaining pin.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — RECOMMENDED STORAGE MAINTENANCE, printed p.37

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The trigger pack itself is not stripped further
deepSteps.action: The pack comes OUT to be cleaned; it does not come APART. Beretta's own limit on this whole chapter is plain — no repairs without proper knowledge or training, no altered parts, no substitute parts that are not Beretta's. Anything the mechanism actually needs goes to the manufacturer or an authorised distributor.
deepSteps.aside: Do not attempt to carry out repairs to any firearm without proper knowledge or training. Do not alter parts or use substitute parts not manufactured by Beretta.
deepSteps.quote: The trigger pack only needs to be disassembled in order to clean the trigger mechanism.
deepSteps.cite: Beretta Semiauto Shotgun User Manual — UQAN3953 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header of every page; the book prints no year) — A300 ULTIMA DISASSEMBLY, printed p.23-25

cleaning.name: CHOKE TUBE & HOUSING
tasks: Choke out, housing brushed and dried
Choke checked clean inside AND outside
Thin film of gun oil on the barrel thread and the choke before it goes back

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Soft patch through to lift combustion residue; brass brush if it needs it
Barrel extension cleaned thoroughly — that is the locking surface
Dry patch, then a lightly oiled cloth over the outside
⛔ Bore checked clear before it goes back on

cleaning.name: GAS CYLINDER, PISTON, MAGAZINE TUBE
tasks: Magazine tube shaft sprayed and cleaned; piston must glide freely on it
Gas cylinder walls brushed with a brass brush, then wiped out
⛔ NEVER oil inside the gas cylinder — these parts run dry

cleaning.name: BREECH BOLT, TRIGGER PACK, RECEIVER (end of season)
tasks: Bolt parts sprayed, dried thoroughly, lightly lubricated
Trigger pack wiped clean; metal parts and the retaining pin lightly oiled
Receiver's internal bolt guides cleaned and lubricated
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges

reassembly: Bolt assembly and operating rod with sleeve onto the magazine tube shaft, ejection port UP.
⛔ Cocking handle struck home until FULLY seated.
Trigger pack in and its retaining pin driven home.
Barrel checked clear and back into the receiver with the piston held in its cylinder; forend adapter, then the forend slid back.
⛔ Magazine cap sleeve back in ITS ORIGINAL ORIENTATION, then the forend cap.
Barrel clamp on, both hex screws tight; choke in and tightened.
Cycle the action and function check before loading.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: the cocking handle must be COMPLETELY seated — Beretta warns a partly-seated handle can dislodge in use. Cycle the bolt several times and confirm it locks open and returns to battery, check the barrel clamp screws are tight, and check the magazine cap sleeve went back the way it came off.
